newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia financing firm sees 500 bln rph from IPO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia financing firm sees 500 bln rph from IPO.

text.p: Indonesian finance firm PT Putra Surya Multidana, whose net profit has risen 19-fold in three years to 1996, said on Friday that it expects to raise 500 billion rupiah from the flotation of 250 million shares in April.

"The net proceeds from the initial public offer (IPO), expected to be around 500 billion rupiah, will be 100 percent used to finance motorcycle and automotive financing," president director Lie Woen Sen told a news conference.

Sen said Putra Surya Multidana, a member of the Putra Surya Perkasa Group, planned to use the proceeds to further expand the firm's core business of financing sales of motorcycles and light commercial vehicles to lower-middle income consumers.
The share offer price was expected to be around 2,000 rupiah, with a nominal price of 500 rupiah, Deswandi Agusman, managing director of brokerage firm PT Peregrine Sewu Securities said.
The firm expected to finance the purchase of around 350,000 motorcycles this year, up from 156,000 in 1996.
It also planned to finance the purchase of some 33,000 light commercial vehicles this year compared with 30,000 last year, Sen said.
The firm's gross lending out reached 1.95 trillion rupiah in 1996 against 435.3 billion rupiah in 1995, 123.7 billion rupiah in 1994 and 8.4 billion rupiah in 1993.
"The sharp jump to 1.9 trillion rupiah in 1996 from only 8.4 billion rupiah in 1993 was only natural, there was nothing wrong against regulations," Sen said commenting the sharp jump.
Meanwhile net profit jumped to 77.94 billion rupiah in 1996 against 21.64 billion rupiah in 1995, 9.13 billion rupiah in 1994 and 3.95 billion rupiah in 1993.
Sen said motorcycle and vehicle consumer financing is and would remain an attractive business in the country as the growth potential is likely to remain strong in the coming years.

"The bad debt rate is also very samll, well below one percent. Many of our consumers are those living in smaller cities and from the lower to middle income brackets. They are more reliable," Sen said.
Sen also said the strong growth could also be seen from the rising number of its branches across the main islands of Java and Bali from zero in 1993 to 34 in 1996.
The number of its employees also grew to 3,583 from only 51 in 1993, Sen said.
Unit sales of motorcycles in Indonesia is expected to reach 1.7 million in 1997 against 1.3 million units, Sen said.
He declined to reveal the expected number of light vehicles unit sales in 1997. The number of light commercial vehicles sold in 1996 was 285,000 units, he said.

As of last year, almost half of the firm's funds came from the government credit programme known as Kredit Usaha Kecil (KUK). The facility offers relatively attractive rates to help small businessmen. The firm declined to give further details.
